evidence_summary: Effects Database identifies the UMI Buzz Tone & Volume Expander and links it to the same marketed/product family as the Conrad Buzz Box, Apollo No. 843, and Applied/Kimberly states. Reverb editorial also identifies Conrad as a UMI Buzz Tone variant. This supports UMI as a physical maker for the later UMI state but does not establish every visually related pedal as UMI-built.

Effects Database catalogs Conrad as a UMI-related marketed state, and Reverb explicitly says the Conrad Buzz Box was also sold as the UMI Buzz Tone and Volume Expander. A 2009 specialist discussion independently observed that the Conrad specimen closely matched the UMI unit while noting the contour-control difference. This supports a UMI product-family relationship without requiring identical production states.

Effects Database places Apollo No. 843 in the same Kimberly/Applied/UMI product-family chain and identifies the Apollo unit as UMI-linked. The record is kept separate from Conrad and Kimberly because a related circuit/product family does not erase distinct marketed states.

Effects Database explicitly distinguishes Kimberly v1 by LIMMCO and v2 by Applied, while the later UMI-linked Apollo/Conrad states connect the broader Buzz Box family to UMI. This record should continue to preserve builder changes instead of treating Kimberly as a single-factory model.

Effects Database groups Audio Designs Fuzzound beside the Applied/Kimberly Buzz Box family, and specialist construction discussion describes it as the same or closely related design. The archive should retain the Applied attribution as a family research result, not infer that every Buzz Box variant used the same exact production run.

Current evidence supports a staged family history: initial Kimberly Buzz Box production by LIMMCO, an Applied stage, and later UMI-linked production represented by UMI Buzz Tone, Conrad, and Apollo. The stages remain distinct because the sources establish family continuity more strongly than they establish exact factory handoff dates for every specimen.

Conrad is best recorded as a distinct marketed identity within the UMI Buzz Tone family rather than as a separate manufacturer. Reverb's historical overview states that the Conrad was also sold as the UMI Buzz Tone and Volume Expander, while Effects Database lists both within the same related family.
